text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
The man renowned to be the thinnest in the world, CLAUDE SEURAT, was born in 1797. Thousands flocked to see him on exhibition in London in 1825 - His chest was just 8 centimetres (3 inches) thick!
English judge and politician JAMES STEPHEN, who while in colonial Melbourne wrote "Adventures Of A Gentleman In Search Of A Horse" and "The Life Of Christ", was born in 1822.
English religious leader and founder of the Salvation Army WILLIAM BOOTH was born in 1829.
American newspaper proprietor JOSEPH PULITZER, who founded the "Pulitzer Prize" for achievements in journalism and literature, was born in 1847.
American playwright and politician CLARE BOOTHE LUCE was born in 1903.
Swedish actor MAX VON SYDOW was born in 1929.
Egyptian actor OMAR SHARIF, whose many films included "Lawrence Of Arabia" and "Doctor Zhivago", was born in 1932 as MICHAEL SHALHOUB.
Australian olympic swimmer and photojournalist KEVIN BERRY, who won gold in Tokyo (butterfly), was born in 1945.
**EVENTS**
1633 : Bananas appeared in British shops and markets for
the first time.
1820 : The first British settlers arrived at Algoa Bay,
South Africa.
1841 : The "New York Tribune" was published for the first
time.
1849 : The safety pin was patented by WALTER HUNT of New
York.
1864 : Archduke MAXIMILIAN of Austria accepted the throne
of Mexico.
1919 : Revolutionary leader EMILIANO ZAPATA was ambushed
and killed by government troops in Mexico.
1921 : SUN YAT-SEN was elected President of China.
1932 : PAUL VON HINDENBURG defeated ADOLF HITLER in the
German Presidential election, polling 19 million votes to HITLER's 13 million.
1944 : Russian troops recaptured Odessa from the Germans
in World War Two.
1956 : Popular American jazz musician NAT KING COLE was
assaulted by racists during a performance in Alabama. He played down the incident, but some blacks criticised his stance, after he'd earlier been targetted by racists when moving into a plush
Los Angeles suburb.
1960 : The United States Senate passed the Civil Rights
Bill.
1963 : The U.S. submarine Thresher sank off Cape Cod in
the Atlantic with the loss of 129 lives.
1974 : GOLDA MEIR resigned as Israeli Prime Minister.
1980 : Spain and Britain agreed to reopen the border
between Gibraltar and Spain, closed in 1969.
1983 : Tasmanian Premier ROBIN GRAY accused the Prime

Minister BOB HAWKE of using an RAAF Mirage jet to spy on the Franklin River dam site. Three months later the High Court upheld Federal government legislation blocking the dam's construction. The High Court ruled that the Federal Government could overrule State laws in order to implement international treaties, in this case a conservation treaty, to which Australia was a signatory.
1989 : Police and rioters clashed in Tiblisi, the capital
of the then Soviet Republic of Georgia. 20 civilians were killed by Soviet special forces.
1989 : NICK FALDO became the first Briton to win the
United States Masters Golf Tournament.
1991 : The Georgian Parliament voted for the 'restoration

of State independence', becoming the latest Soviet Republic to seek to break away from central control. The declaration came on the 2nd anniversary (see 1989 above) of the Tiblisi riot that left 20 people dead.
1994 : NATO warplanes launched air strikes for the first
time on Serb forces advancing on the Bosnian Moslem town of Gorazde, a U.N.-declared "safe area".
